title: Normalize token attribution for multipart requests with async retries
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Intermittent client reconnects and asynchronous retry semantics can cause multipart/multi-fragment requests to be double-counted or misattributed in the usage ledger. This ticket standardizes fragment-level attribution and introduces idempotent commit semantics so retries and out-of-order fragment arrival do not inflate token consumption or incorrectly charge quotas.

Background: We observe recurring incidents where long inputs split into multiple fragments (prefix frames, streamed attachments, or chunked tokenization outputs) are re-sent by clients or replayed by edge proxies. Our current pipeline attributes tokens at several places (gateway, tokenizer, and ledger) and relies on per-request idempotency alone. When fragments are retried or arrive out of sequence, partial commits and race conditions have resulted in: (1) duplicated input token counts, (2) output tokens billed to the wrong request id after mid-stream model switch, and (3) quota breaches triggered incorrectly leading to throttles/premature rate-limit responses.

This work aligns billing behavior with user expectations: a single logical request (potentially multipart) should be billed exactly once for each token produced/consumed regardless of retries or transport reordering.
acceptance_criteria: Fragment-level canonicalization: each fragment has a stable fingerprint and sequence index; ledger only credits unique fingerprints per logical request.
Idempotent commit API: a two-phase commit where token contributions are tentatively recorded and only finalized once a terminal fragment sequence is received or a configurable timeout elapses.
Rate limiter integration: quota checks use tentative reservations that are subtracted at finalize time; no double-counting on retries.
End-to-end tests: deterministic test harness reproduces reconnect/retry scenarios and shows zero double-charges for 1000 simulated retry events.
Monitoring: new dashboards show fragment duplication rate, finalize latency, and frequency of forced timeouts with alerts at >0.5% duplication.
Backward compatibility: clients that do not send fragment sequence metadata still get correct billing (slow-path fingerprinting), but with increased finalize latency documented.
Migration: reconciliation job corrects historical overcharges for a targeted window (script produces audit report for finance review).
steps_to_reproduce: Configure client to split a 6k token prompt into 3 fragments and enable automatic retry on connection loss.
Simulate network drop after fragment 2 and let client retry fragments 2-3 with a new connection id but same request id.
Observe ledger entries: currently we see two separate reservations and two final credits for input tokens for the same logical request.
Trigger a mid-stream model switch (fallback model) and confirm output tokens are attributed to the wrong request id in the current pipeline.
Run existing reconciliation script and verify it cannot deterministically collapse the duplicates without additional fragment metadata.
implementation_notes: Add per-fragment fields: fragment_seq (int), fragment_hash (sha256 as hex), tentative=true/false flag stored in ledger rows (tentative flag implemented as separate column).
Gateway: compute fragment_hash before forwarding to tokenizer; attach fingerprint to in-flight frames and include in streaming resume headers.
Tokenizer: emit token_count and fragment_hash; if tokenizer cannot determine deterministic hash (legacy client), fallback to content-hash of normalized text with a note in logs.

Ledger: dedupe on (request_id, fragment_hash) when applying finalized credits. Introduce finalize endpoint that moves tentative reservations to committed tokens and releases tentative locks on quota accounting.

Rate limiter: consume tentative tokens from quota pool when fragment first arrives; finalize will persist final charge. If finalize fails due to quota, run a predefined rollback to unit-test behavior and alert ops.
Reconciliation job: new offline job that groups tentative fragments and uses fragment_hash and sequence metadata to collapse duplicates for windows where finalize did not complete.
Feature flag: behind meter.fragment-idempotency; default off for canary rollout.
work_log: 2025-11-03 - Triage: Priya Nair - Identified as regression impacting monthly billing audits; elevated to P0.
2025-11-05 - Design kickoff: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Marina Kovács - Captured split/fingerprint approach; agreed two-phase commit model.
2025-11-08 - Spike: Alex Chen - Built prototype on dev-gateway; fragment_hash collisions negligible in preliminary tests (0/100k).
2025-11-11 - Review: Security and privacy reviewed fingerprint approach; salt per-tenant recommended to prevent cross-tenant fragment correlation.
2025-11-13 - Implementation: Started ledger schema migration branch (WIP) - added tentative_token_count column and uniqueness constraint on (request_id, fragment_hash).

2025-11-16 - Integration test: Ran streaming retry harness with 10k sessions; duplicate rate reduced from 1.4% to 0.02% on prototype but observed a 3% increase in finalize latency under load. Added performance tuning action item.
2025-11-17 - Blocked: Waiting on tokenizer patch to emit fragment_hash reliably (ENG-84533).
2025-11-18 - Design refinement: Added slow-path fingerprinting and admin reconciliation endpoint for finance requests.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: fragment_hash collisions could incorrectly collapse distinct fragments -> Mitigation: include fragment_seq and per-tenant salt in fingerprint; reject finalize if sequence gaps detected.

Risk: increased finalize latency under heavy load leading to perceived quota delays -> Mitigation: optimistic tentative reservations sized small, backpressure on gateway, and canary rollout with performance monitoring.
Risk: migration of ledger schema causes DB migration lock -> Mitigation: online migration with write-path feature flag and small batch backfill during low-traffic windows.
Risk: clients without sequence metadata might get slower billing -> Mitigation: document expected behavior and provide SDK update with auto-fragment headers.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Deploy feature-flagged gateway + tokenizer changes to staging; run synthetic harness for 100k reconnects.
Phase 2 (canary): Enable for 5% of production accounts with monitoring on finalize latency and duplication rate.
Phase 3: Gradually expand to all accounts over 72 hours if duplication <0.1% and finalize P95 < 3s.
Phase 4: Run reconciliation job for historical 7-day window and surface finance audit report.
notes_for_finance: Produce audit CSV with columns: request_id, fragment_hash, tentative_tokens, finalized_tokens, timestamp, action_taken
If reconciliation reduces charges for customers in the run window, create credit memos and attach audit CSV for review.
